text:
maria: FYI eu-central1 NVMe read p99 jumped -> lots of gpu attach failures. anyone else seeing this?

sre-bot: ALERT: nodepool/eu-central1-nvme read p99=310ms over 5m, affected: gpu-attach.

alex: noticed many fscrypt re-encrypt workers started shortly after last-night KMS rotation. /scratch scans hitting NVMe.

jamal: ugh. who triggered rotation? coordinated re-encrypt could explain cluster-wide IO spike.

kevin: key-ops did. re-encrypt is policy-run and should be low priority but clearly saturated reads. pausing rollout now.

maria: sample from gnode-137 logs:
```
Mar 23 02:12:09 gnode-137 fscrypt[3281]: re-encrypt start /scratch (/dev/nvme0n1p1)
Mar 23 02:12:13 kernel: nvme 0000:3b:00.0: read latency: 65ms -> 412ms
Mar 23 02:12:40 kubelet: attach failed: ProvisionTimeout
```

alex: mitigation plan: (1) pause key-ops rollout (kevin) (2) cap fscrypt IO via cgroup/systemd IOWeight (3) route new gpu attaches away from eu-central1 for 15m.

kevin: paused rollout. will add annotation to avoid auto-resume.

maria: throttled live workers on sampled node: `sudo systemctl set-property fscrypt.service IOWeight=10`; p99 dropped to ~30ms, attach retries succeeding.

jamal: can we schedule re-encrypts with IO caps and an "IO headroom" preflight? file follow-up.

kevin: cost note: routing to us-west2 adds short-term egress/latency cost (~+10%) but kept SLA. recommend adding interlock in key-ops.

sre-bot: ACTIONS logged: key-ops paused, in-flight workers signalled, regional routing adjusted.

maria: filing INFRA-7901: "KMS re-encrypt -> IO headroom interlock + throttles + rollback play". monitoring eu-central1 now :white_check_mark:
